title: Impact Resistant Cargo Lining Panels with Integrated Light Strip Housing
abstract: A tougher cargo lining panel that carries the compartment light strip inside its own moulding, cutting the panel damage rate that short-sector baggage handling had been driving.

sections.reason: Cargo lining panel replacement was the highest volume cabin spares line on the type. Panels crack at the lower edge where baggage is dragged across the sill, and the surface-mounted light strip above the sill is knocked off its clips. Operators flying five or more sectors a day were replacing an average of 3.1 panels per aircraft per year against a fleet average of 0.9, and two operators had asked for a design answer rather than a spares discount.
sections.description: The lower cargo lining panels are re-moulded in a glass-reinforced compound with a thicker lower edge and a rolled return, and the compartment light strip is carried inside a recess in the panel rather than on clips above it. Panel D2550118547929 replaces the previous item, the light assembly D2550118482429 is re-housed and its lens is flush with the panel face, and anchor nuts EN513769-76 hold the panel to the existing frame brackets so that no structure is drilled. The panel trim 60DQ and the light assembly 44DL keep their identifiers. Revised detail is on drawing D25501190381. The panels are fitted in the forward and aft cargo compartments, zones 111, 131 and 141.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 9.6 kg per aircraft across both compartments, distributed close to the centre of gravity. Electrical load is unchanged. The panels are not interchangeable with the previous standard because the light strip has no separate clips in the new arrangement, so a compartment must be converted as a set. Loadable cargo volume is unchanged. Illustrated parts content for the cargo compartment needs re-issue and the lining removal and installation tasks change because the light connector is now behind the panel.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the CIRRANE-13 production line at MSN C00678 in March 2024. Retrofit through Service Bulletin CRN-25-1018 is offered per compartment and takes one night stop for the aft compartment. The CIRRANE-11 keeps the previous panel because its shorter compartment uses a different panel set.

type_data.balance_impact: Close to the reference CG, no reportable shift
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00678, cargo compartment fit-out unchanged in duration
